title: China Blocks Meta's $2 Billion Acquisition of AI Agent Startup Manus
description: China's economic watchdog blocked Meta's $2 billion acquisition of AI agent startup Manus. The deal was largely complete and Manus was already integrated into some of Meta's tools, but Beijing canceled the acquisition without explaining their decision.
author: Robert Hart

title: Elon Musk Drops Fraud Claims Against OpenAI Before Trial
description: Elon Musk voluntarily dropped fraud claims against OpenAI and Sam Altman before the trial began. The federal judge granted Musk's request to streamline the case, focusing instead on ensuring OpenAI adheres to its public charitable mission.
author: Robert Hart

title: Microsoft and OpenAI's Famed AGI Agreement is Dead
description: The landmark AGI agreement between Microsoft and OpenAI has been terminated, fundamentally changing their partnership structure. The original agreement gave Microsoft exclusive rights to OpenAI's technology until AGI was achieved.
author: Elizabeth Lopatto

title: AI-Designed Car is Taking Shape
description: A vehicle designed entirely by AI is moving from concept to reality. The article showcases images of the AI-designed car, highlighting how generative AI is revolutionizing automotive design and engineering.
author: Robert Hart

title: OpenAI's Super PAC Might Be Funding a 'News' Site Staffed by AI Reporters
description: Investigation reveals that OpenAI's super PAC appears to be funding The Wire by Acutus, a suspiciously pro-AI news site where most 'reporters' appear to be bots. One reporter, Michael Chen, likely doesn't exist.
author: Terrence O'Brien

title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman Apologized to Town of Tumbler Ridge
description: Sam Altman personally apologized to the Canadian town of Tumbler Ridge after a school shooting suspect described violent scenarios to ChatGPT. While OpenAI banned the account, they did not alert law enforcement about the person.
author: Jay Peters

title: Sinceerly Uses AI to Make Your AI Writing Sound Less Like You're Using AI
description: A satirical Chrome extension called Sinceerly promises to banish AI writing patterns like the em-dash, remove phrases that are dead giveaways of AI, and even introduce typos. Developer Dan Horwitz calls it an 'anti-Grammarly' commentary on AI detection.
author: Terrence O'Brien

title: Suno AI Music Now Available on Android Auto
description: AI music generation platform Suno is now available on Android Auto, with CarPlay support in development. The integration currently supports search, library, explore, and playback control, allowing users to stream AI-generated music while driving.
author: Terrence O'Brien

title: The Biggest AI Trends and Tools Emerging in April 2026
description: AI is evolving beyond chatbots into autonomous execution systems. Key trends include coding agents becoming full software engineers, TurboQuant KV cache compression achieving 6x memory reduction, multi-agent systems replacing linear workflows, and AI runtime layers emerging as new infrastructure category.
author: Vishal Mysore

title: DeepSeek V4—almost on the frontier, a fraction of the price
description: Chinese AI lab DeepSeek released V4-Pro and V4-Flash preview models. Simon Willison provides analysis of their performance and pricing positioning relative to frontier models.
author: Simon Willison

title: honker: Postgres NOTIFY/LISTEN semantics for SQLite
description: Rust SQLite extension implementing Postgres-style queue and stream functionality with transactional outbox pattern. Enables Kafka-style durable streams and queue operations in SQLite.
author: Simon Willison

title: An update on recent Claude Code quality reports
description: Anthropic released a postmortem on Claude Code quality issues over the past two months. Key bug: clearing thinking from idle sessions kept happening every turn instead of once, causing forgetful behavior. Important lessons for agentic system builders.
author: Simon Willison

title: Serving the For You feed - Bluesky's architecture
description: Deep dive into how spacecowboy's Bluesky feed serves 72,000 users from a single Go process with SQLite on a gaming PC (16 cores, 96GB RAM, 4TB NVMe). Total cost: $30/month. Stores 90 days of data in 419GB SQLite database.
author: Simon Willison

title: Extract PDF text in your browser with LiteParse for the web
description: Simon ported LlamaIndex's LiteParse PDF extraction tool to run entirely in the browser using the same libraries as the Node.js version.
author: Simon Willison

title: GPT-5.5 pelican generation via Codex backdoor API
description: Testing GPT-5.5's image generation capabilities with the classic 'pelican riding a bicycle' prompt. Found it to be fast, effective and highly capable.
author: Simon Willison
